quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.
Always shift all the way to neutral first.
Accelerate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When downshifting, move down one gear at a time. Slowly release the clutch between each shift.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver sees you.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car. This position makes you visible in the driver's rearview mirror where they are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: The best way to brake hard in a straight line is to:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes and lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straight road, you can stop fastest by using both brakes. Do not lock either brake.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far back on the seat so you can keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not just hold you in place. Your arms should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Relax your grip on the handle grips.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handle grips firmly. Ease off the throttle and go straight. Slowly brake on the good tire only. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles curves the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be used on curves.
Should use the shoulder when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles.

questions.question: Studies show that motorcycles with headlights on during the day are:

options.text: Not as easy to see as other vehicles.
More visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
Often confusing to other drivers.
Less safe than with headlights off.

questions.correctAnswerText: More visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. A motorcycle with its headlight on during the day is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Give a good view of the shoulder.
Make it hard to see road hazards.
Invite other vehicles to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that lets you see others and lets them see you. Do not stay in another driver's blind spot for long periods.

questions.question: Your lane position should help you:

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
Stop other drivers from passing you.
Get to your destination as fast as possible.
Stay in other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: A good lane position protects your lane and shows other drivers your intentions.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: On short trips.
On long trips.
After at least one hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts out.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcyclist should tell the passenger to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Hold onto the seat.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger safety instructions before you leave. Ask them to get on only after you start the engine. They should sit as close to you as possible without crowding you and hold your waist, hips, or belt firmly. They should keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when the bike is stopped.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Begin slowing down sooner than usual.
Begin slowing down later than usual.
Brake harder than usual to stop quickly.
Brake gently to avoid overworking the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Begin slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger in a sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle. This extra weight means your motorcycle will need more distance to stop. Start slowing down earlier than you normally would.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected if they are wearing:

options.text: A jacket with exposed arms.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. Wear tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Choose footwear with low heels that won't catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves or gloves made from other durable materials protect your hands in a crash and help you grip the controls better.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: Make it easier for other drivers to see you.
Can be distracting.
Don't help with your visibility.
Are not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make it easier for other drivers to see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a brightly-colored helmet. It will protect your head in a crash, and the bright color helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It takes less time to speed up, but more time to stop.
It takes more time to speed up and to stop.
It takes more time to speed up, but less time to stop.
It takes less time to speed up and to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to speed up and to stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle slower to speed up and slower to stop compared to riding alone.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white backgrounds and black lettering show road rules like speed limits. You must follow the rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a benefit of riding in a tight group?

options.text: It uses less space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is less likely to get separated.
Riders reach their destination faster in a tight group than a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders reach their destination faster in a tight group than a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a tight group is better than riding spread out because the group takes less road space, is easier to see, and is less likely to get separated at traffic lights or during passes. The speed is the same.

questions.question: If you are not traveling slowly enough when shifting into a lower gear, what could happen?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jolt and the rear tire may skid.
The horn may go off.
Your motorcycle may jolt and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jolt and a warning light will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jolt and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you are going too fast when you shift into a lower gear, your motorcycle will jolt and the rear tire may skid. This can cause you to lose control. Always slow down enough before shifting into a lower gear.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of a crash, you should:

options.text: Not use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Look only five feet ahead of your motorcycle while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, make sure others can see you. Use your turn signals, brake lights, and correct lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you. Always be ready to avoid hazards.

questions.question: When stopping:

options.text: Apply the rear brake first.
Apply the front brake first.
Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, either front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: What will protect your eyes from the wind?

options.text: Goggles
Windshield
Sunglasses
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect a rider's eyes from the wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, what does it mean?

options.text: Plans to turn left.
Is about to stop.
Plans to turn right.
Is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals when they don't have mechanical turn signals. A left arm bent at the elbow and pointing upward means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.
Is less effective than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not an adequate substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: In general, how should riders choose their lane position?

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent monotony.
Choose a lane position that maximizes their space cushion.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that maximizes their space cushion.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. The safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space around you and makes other drivers see you most easily.
